observationsNotFindings: The recomputed fixture audit is the best evidence artifact I have seen in this sweep. Rather than asserting that the eleven classes have authored bytes, it states counts that can be reproduced from disk - 11 classes, 11 primaries, 17 files, 0 digest mismatches - and I reproduced all four by opening every file. Most artifacts in this family make claims about other artifacts; this one makes a claim about the filesystem and stakes checkable numbers on it.

The disposition that matters most is the one that did not move. An accepted naming candidate and an authored harness specification could easily have been read as giving OBL-NT-11-EXECUTION an owner, and the join explicitly declines: no live file-08 DR-G* owns identity-namespace negative-test execution, so the obligation stays open. That is the whole difference between a proposal and a live gate, and the artifact holds it.

Neither 27 nor 31 appears anywhere in this join, even though the naming candidate it lands proposes exactly those cardinalities. Keeping the proposed numbers out of the measurement is what stops a naming proposal from leaking into a leftover measurement, and it is worth noting because the two artifacts were reviewed minutes apart and could easily have drifted together.

DR-103 occurs zero times, which is the strongest possible form of not stealing that row's leftover given that all seventeen audited fixtures physically live under the DR-103 fixture tree. The audit takes their digests as evidence that bytes exist without asserting anything about DR-103's obligations.
